title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 28
paragraphs: This whole land I have described has such an exceedingly severe climate that for eight months of the year there is frost so hard as to be intolerable. During these months, if you pour out water you cannot make mud—you can only do so by lighting a fire. The sea is frozen, and the whole Cimmerian Bosphorus, so that the Scythians settled within the trench make expeditions and drive their wagons over into the country of the Sindians. So it continues to be winter for eight months, and even for the remaining four months it is cold in those parts. This winter is different in character from all the winters in other parts of the world. For in it there is no rain worth speaking of at the usual season for rain, whereas in summer it rains continually; and thunder does not come at the time it does in other countries, but is very frequent in summer. If thunder comes in winter, it is marvelled at as a prodigy; likewise if an earthquake occurs, whether in summer or winter, it is accounted a prodigy in Scythia. Horses can endure this winter, but neither mules nor asses can bear it at all—whereas in other countries, horses if they stand in frost lose their limbs by mortification, while asses and mules endure it.
